parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Maple Ridge · Whonnock Lake and the Fraser River
Whonnock is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Maple Ridge doesn’t publish a boundary for it.

The City’s Whonnock page lists Selvey Park, Whonnock Lake Park and Whonnock Lake Centre as the area’s facilities, and its heritage buildings sit along River Road, 272 Street and Lougheed Highway. The City says Whonnock remains a rural residential area where many people have horses and maintain small tree and fruit farms.
The City says the name comes from the local First Nation word meaning “place of the hump-back salmon.”

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Maple Ridge and School District 42.
General information only.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Whonnock

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
Chapter 3 of the Official Community Plan sets out the rural designations for land beyond the Urban Area Boundary. No City statement that I found lists Whonnock by name.

Updates to the Official Community Plan went through in November 2025, along with area plan updates covering Albion, Hammond, Silver Valley and Town Centre, according to the City. Whonnock has no area plan that I found.

Past the Urban Area Boundary, the Official Community Plan from the City describes three rural residential designations. In Rural Residential, lots are generally about 2 acres (0.8 hectares) when community water is available and about 4.9 acres (2.0 hectares) when water is on site. In Suburban Residential the general lot is about 1 acre (0.4 hectares), and Estate Suburban Residential lots are generally 0.4 hectares too.

ALR: I did not find an official statement placing Agricultural Land Reserve land inside Whonnock. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the Agricultural Land Commission map.
I found no flood designation written for Whonnock. The City publishes a Be Flood Ready guide, a Fraser River Floodplain Map and a monitoring page for river levels.
Rainfall and water levels on the Fraser River, Kanaka Creek and the North and South Alouette River are monitored by the City.
Some parts of Maple Ridge are exposed to landslides and debris flows, the City says. It adds that landslides can happen when warm weather melts the snowpack.
I found no slope area named for Whonnock, so check the City’s maps for the exact address.

Whonnock is without a West Coast Express station. There are two West Coast Express stops in Maple Ridge, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station; the five daily trips leave Maple Ridge in the morning and come back in the evening, Monday to Friday.

Where is Whonnock?
Whonnock is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Maple Ridge doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
The City’s Whonnock page lists Selvey Park, Whonnock Lake Park and Whonnock Lake Centre as its facilities, with heritage buildings along River Road, 272 Street and Lougheed Highway.
How do I get around from Whonnock?

Route 749, Ruskin / Haney Place, is a loop. It leaves Haney Place, heads for 280 Street at Lougheed Highway, then returns to Haney Place. Outbound it travels on Dewdney Trunk Road, then 284 Street and finally 116 Avenue; inbound it takes Lougheed Highway, then 272 Street and finally Dewdney Trunk Road.
Timetable dates: 749, effective June 8, 2026. Check the current timetable.

No West Coast Express station exists in Whonnock. The two Maple Ridge stops are Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, and the train runs five trips a day from Monday to Friday, heading out in the morning and returning in the evening.
Which schools are in Whonnock?
Whonnock Elementary, K-7, is at 27471 112 Avenue. I found no secondary school in Whonnock; Garibaldi Secondary, Grades 8-12, is at 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
School District 42 (SD42)
What parks and library are there?
Whonnock Lake Park and Whonnock Lake Centre are at 27871 113 Avenue, and Selvey Park is at 27101 106 Avenue.
At 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road is the Maple Ridge Public Library, the sole branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library in Maple Ridge.
What plan covers Whonnock?
I found no area plan for Whonnock. The Official Community Plan’s rural designations apply to land outside the Urban Area Boundary.
Is Whonnock in a floodplain or on a slope?
I found no flood or slope statement written for Whonnock in the City’s sources.

Floodplain maps are published by the City for the North and South Alouette River and for the Fraser River. The City describes a floodplain map as outlining the area expected, on average, to flood once every 200 years.
Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
What are the homes and lots like?
The City describes Whonnock as a rural residential area where many people have horses and maintain small tree and fruit farms.

Under the City’s Official Community Plan, rural residential land outside the Urban Area Boundary falls into three designations. Lots in Suburban Residential are generally 0.4 hectares (about 1 acre), as are Estate Suburban Residential lots. Rural Residential is larger: generally 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) with water on site, or, with community water available, 0.8 hectares (about 2 acres).
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map
